stem: A 5-year-old child presents to the emergency department with fever, petechial rash, irritability, headache, and neck stiffness. You suspect meningitis and are discussing lumbar puncture with the mother, who is worried about spinal cord injury. Which statement is correct about the anatomy relevant to lumbar puncture?

options.text: In the lateral decubitus position with the child tightly curled, the spinal cord ends at the iliac crest and is therefore not in danger of being damaged when the needle is introduced at L3/4
The anatomical landmark across the iliac crests corresponds to L3/L4 which is below the level where the spinal cord ends and therefore it is not in danger of being damaged
The needle enters the epidural space when inserted to sample cerebrospinal fluid and therefore the spinal cord is not in danger of being damaged
The spinal cord in children is shorter and thinner than in adults and therefore it is safe to introduce the needle at L1/2 and not endanger the spinal cord

explanation: Lumbar puncture is performed below the end of the spinal cord, which in children is typically around L1–L2, and the intercristal line (line across the iliac crests) approximates the L3/4 level, making this a safe site for needle insertion.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect: the spinal cord does not end at the iliac crest.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: the iliac crest line corresponds to about L3/4, below the end of the spinal cord.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: cerebrospinal fluid is sampled from the subarachnoid space, not the epidural space.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: L1/2 is too high and may risk contact with the spinal cord.

source.questionTextHtml:
A 5 year old child has presented to the emergency department because of fever and a petechial rash. She is noted to be irritable and complaining of a headache and sore neck to her mother during the review.

You think she may have meningitis and therefore you wish to consult her mother before performing a lumbar puncture on the child. Her mother asks you a number of questions regarding the lumbar puncture as she is anxious you may damage her daughter’s spinal cord.

You advise her that:

Instructions

Question 4 - 6 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 5-year old girl is brought in by her mother to see you because her teacher has been concerned that she has been having ‘day-dreams’ in choir practise and also during class. Her mother has also noted ‘day dreams’ which have been occurring mid-sentence associated with staring off in the distance. The ‘day dreams’ last a few seconds and then she is back to normal and continues on with her sentence. She doesn’t fall and doesn’t get sleepy after the events. She has no colour change. The girl is otherwise developmentally normal and got a good mid-year report from school. On examination her height and weight are on the 75

th

centile. She has a completely normal examination. You get the patient to blow up a balloon in your office and she has a staring spell that lasts 5seconds before she completely recovers.
